SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #19 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. On most maps, which direction is at the top? (1 mark)
   A. South
   B. North
   C. West
   D. East

2. On a map of a village, the church is to the east of the school. On the map, where is the church drawn? (1 mark)
   A. On the right of the school
   B. Above the school
   C. On the left of the school
   D. Below the school

3. Which direction is Mombasa from Nairobi on a map of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. South-east
   B. North-west
   C. West
   D. North

4. Which ocean is found on the south-eastern side of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Arctic Ocean
   B. Atlantic Ocean
   C. Indian Ocean
   D. Pacific Ocean

5. What does the size of a county mean? (1 mark)
   A. The area of land it covers
   B. The number of schools in it
   C. The number of roads in it
   D. The number of people in it

6. Which is the largest county in Kenya by area? (1 mark)
   A. Mombasa
   B. Turkana
   C. Kisumu
   D. Nairobi

7. Which of these is a physical feature? (1 mark)
   A. A bridge
   B. A lake
   C. A school
   D. A road

8. What is a river? (1 mark)
   A. Water flowing along a channel from high land to low land
   B. A flat plain
   C. A big lake
   D. A steep hill

9. What is a plateau? (1 mark)
   A. High land that is flat on top
   B. A coast
   C. A deep valley
   D. A river

10. During which season do fishermen often dry fish in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Rainy season
   B. No season
   C. Dry season
   D. Flood season

11. Which drink is likely to sell more during the hot season? (1 mark)
   A. Hot porridge
   B. Hot tea
   C. Cold drinks
   D. Hot soup

12. How can a historic place help a county to earn money? (1 mark)
   A. By selling its walls
   B. By bringing visitors who pay fees and buy things
   C. By closing to everybody
   D. By stopping all jobs

13. Which place in Nairobi shows traditional homes and dances of many communities? (1 mark)
   A. Lamu Old Town
   B. Fort Jesus
   C. Gede Ruins
   D. Bomas of Kenya

14. Why do tourists visit historic places? (1 mark)
   A. To cut trees
   B. To buy soap
   C. To plant maize
   D. To learn about the past and enjoy the sights

15. Which of these shows interdependence? (1 mark)
   A. A child eating alone
   B. A man refusing help
   C. Farmer sells maize and buys clothes from a tailor
   D. A woman sleeping

16. Which is a way of showing appreciation for others? (1 mark)
   A. Saying thank you
   B. Breaking their tools
   C. Laughing at their work
   D. Ignoring their help

17. Which group depends on teachers? (1 mark)
   A. Only teachers
   B. Everyone who wants to learn
   C. Only drivers
   D. Only farmers

18. Which of these is not a reason for crowded areas? (1 mark)
   A. Jobs in a town
   B. Good roads
   C. Very little rain and no water
   D. Fertile soil

19. Which area is most likely to be sparsely populated? (1 mark)
   A. A busy town
   B. A very dry area with little rain
   C. A fertile highland
   D. A lakeshore with fish

20. Why must a key be included on a dot map? (1 mark)
   A. So that people know what each dot stands for
   B. So that colours are hidden
   C. So that it looks old
   D. So that the map is longer

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. What is a compass used for? (2 marks)

22. State three road safety rules for a rainy day. (3 marks)

23. Give two reasons why we need to know the location of our county. (2 marks)

24. Describe how to draw a dot map showing population distribution in your county. (4 marks)

25. Explain the difference between clustered and scattered settlement. (3 marks)

26. Describe three ways in which pupils can take part in conserving a historic place near their school. (3 marks)

27. Explain how the Tana River helps people in Kenya. (3 marks)

28. Describe three problems that crowded areas can have and one way of reducing each. (5 marks)

29. Explain the meaning of population distribution. (2 marks)

30. A weather chart for a week shows: Mon sunny, Tue sunny, Wed rainy, Thu cloudy, Fri rainy, Sat sunny, Sun cloudy. How many days were sunny, rainy and cloudy? (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #19 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — North
   Maps are drawn with north at the top unless a north arrow shows otherwise.

2. A — On the right of the school
   East is on the right when north is at the top.

3. A — South-east
   Mombasa lies to the south-east of Nairobi.

4. C — Indian Ocean
   Kenya's coast is on the Indian Ocean.

5. A — The area of land it covers
   Size means the area of land, not the population.

6. B — Turkana
   Turkana is the largest county by land area.

7. B — A lake
   A lake is natural. The others are built by people.

8. A — Water flowing along a channel from high land to low land
   Rivers flow along channels towards a lake or an ocean.

9. A — High land that is flat on top
   A plateau is a raised area with a flat top.

10. C — Dry season
   Dry sunny days are best for drying fish.

11. C — Cold drinks
   People are thirsty and feel hot, so they buy cold drinks.

12. B — By bringing visitors who pay fees and buy things
   Visitors spend money on tickets, guides and crafts.

13. D — Bomas of Kenya
   The Bomas of Kenya is a cultural centre in Nairobi.

14. D — To learn about the past and enjoy the sights
   Tourism brings income to the local people.

15. C — Farmer sells maize and buys clothes from a tailor
   The farmer and tailor depend on each other.

16. A — Saying thank you
   Thanking people shows we value them.

17. B — Everyone who wants to learn
   Teachers help children learn to read and write, which everybody needs.

18. C — Very little rain and no water
   Dryness with no water makes areas sparse.

19. B — A very dry area with little rain
   Dry areas make farming and water supply hard.

20. A — So that people know what each dot stands for
   Without a key we cannot read the dots.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: A compass is used to find direction. Its needle points to north.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for finding direction, 1 mark for the needle pointing north.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not cross flooded roads, wear bright or reflective clothes, and walk facing traffic if there is no pavement.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct rule.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: To plan journeys and to know which counties are next to us. Accept sharing resources.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible reason.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw the county boundary. Decide how many people one dot stands for. Put more dots where more people live and fewer dots where few live. Add a title and key.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clustered means homes are close together in a group, for example around a town. Scattered means homes are far apart from each other.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for a clear contrast.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sweep and pick up litter, report damage to an adult, and tell others why the place is important.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: It supplies water, its dams produce electric power, and its water is used for irrigation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct use.

28. (5 marks)
   Answer: Shortage of houses: build more houses. Litter: organise cleaning and waste collection. Traffic: improve roads and public transport. Award marks for each problem and each solution.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each problem/solution pair, up to 5 marks.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is how the people are spread out over an area, showing where many people live and where few live.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for spread of people, 1 mark for many and few.

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 sunny days, 2 rainy days and 2 cloudy days.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct count. Check: 3 + 2 + 2 = 7 days.
